## TL;DR

Updated the Android Hub, Android dev publish, and macOS Hub workflows to use explicit SDK setup and runner temporary paths. The Android setup actions now receive an explicit empty additional-package list, while required Android 36 platform and 36.0.0 build tools are installed with `sdkmanager` in build/release jobs. macOS jobs now export temp-derived paths from their first step through `$GITHUB_ENV`. I also fixed the inline prerelease shell comparisons that triggered ShellCheck SC2193 and added regression coverage for Android package configuration and macOS job-level `runner` context usage. The requested scoped `repoos check` passes.

## Work and rationale

The Android workflow used `android-actions/setup-android@v3` twice without a `packages` input. The dev publishing workflow did the same and already had a later explicit `sdkmanager` command. To prevent reliance on action defaults, each setup step now sets `packages: ""`. In the Android Hub workflow, each job that builds an APK now follows setup with an explicit install of `platforms;android-36` and `build-tools;36.0.0`. The release verification step invokes `aapt` from the installed build-tools directory, so the explicit installation preserves that requirement as well as the platform needed by Gradle. The dev publish job retains its existing SDK manager command, which already installs platform 36 and build tools 36.0.0.

The setup-android documentation currently describes `platform-tools` as its default package and says later packages can be installed manually. The failure context describes the observed `@v3` execution reporting a missing `tools` package. The implementation avoids dependence on that discrepancy by making the requested additional-package list explicit on every call and installing the project packages separately. The action's command-line tools and license setup remain provided by the action.

GitHub does not allow the `runner` context in job-level `env`. The macOS build-and-test job now writes both `REPOOS_MACOS_DERIVED_DATA` and `REPOOS_MACOS_XCRESULT_DIR` to `$GITHUB_ENV` from its first step, using the runner-provided `$RUNNER_TEMP` shell variable. Its build and test commands therefore continue to use the same directories. The release job independently initializes `REPOOS_MACOS_DERIVED_DATA`, because GitHub Actions jobs have separate environments. Later packaging commands continue to use `$RUNNER_TEMP` directly for their temporary DMG and notarization files.

Both Android and macOS prerelease checks previously embedded the GitHub expression directly in a shell `[[ ... == *-* ]]` comparison. `actionlint`/ShellCheck reported SC2193 for these generated scripts. Each step now injects the chosen tag into a `RELEASE_TAG` environment variable and checks that variable for a hyphen. This retains the intended prerelease behavior while removing the expression from shell source.

A test in the regular Vitest suite reads these workflow files and requires every setup-android action occurrence to be immediately followed by an explicit empty `packages` input. It also detects `runner.*` expressions in a macOS job-level `env` block. Documentation in the macOS release runbook and Android dev update notes records the temp-directory and SDK installation conventions.

## Approaches tried

I first ran `actionlint` against all three workflows to confirm the reported macOS expression errors and identify both SC2193 warnings. I consulted the upstream setup-android action documentation to confirm the `packages` input behavior and manual-install path. I initially put the guard test in `src/core`, but this repository's Vitest configuration only discovers `src/ui-app/tests/**/*.test.ts`; I moved it into that suite before checking the normal runner. I also ran the focused test directly and corrected its text matching after the first assertion exposed an overly broad regular expression.

The first required scoped check exercised remote validation successfully, but the local format gate failed on the new test file and skipped dependent gates. I ran the repository formatter and reran the exact scoped check. The final run passed. A separate `actionlint` invocation on the three changed workflow files also passed with no expression or ShellCheck warnings. Running `actionlint` over the whole workflow directory emits a separate existing SC2193 warning in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which this task does not change; no expression errors were reported there.

## Challenges and blockers

The action documentation describes the current default as `platform-tools`, while the supplied incident report attributes the observed failure to a request for the removed `tools` package. Pin behavior and docs may have changed over time, but explicit `packages: ""` makes this workflow deterministic regardless. The actual macOS Xcode build, notarization, and GitHub Release upload cannot be proven from the local environment. No release, tag push, or publish was triggered, as required. Confirmation of successful GitHub runs remains for after the change lands.

The `repoos check` command itself created its normal WIP checkpoint commit when preparing the tree for its remote runner; I did not manually stage or commit files. The check completed successfully on that checked tree.

## Key learnings

For GitHub Actions SDK setup, explicitly declare action package inputs and install project-specific SDK packages in a visible `sdkmanager` step. For workflow portability, runner-specific paths should be materialized through `$RUNNER_TEMP` in step execution and exported via `$GITHUB_ENV` when later steps need them. Every job must initialize its own environment values. Finally, keeping GitHub expressions out of inline shell comparisons improves both ShellCheck's analysis and the safety/readability of generated scripts.
